### Santo Domingo: gateway to the Caribbean!

The Dominican Republic's principal city, described as the oldest city in the Americas, is known as the gateway to the Caribbean and the cultural capital of the Americas. Santo Domingo is inseparable from the history of the conquest of the New World. The great explorer Christopher Columbus is said to have found his final resting place here, with his remains held in the giant lighthouse beside the Caribbean Sea. It is believed that the first paved roads, university and Christian cathedral on American soil were established in Santo Domingo.

The Ozama River divides Santo Domingo into two parts. The western section is considered the capital's business and cultural centre, while the eastern section (Santo Domingo Oriental) is described as historic. The most interesting areas for visitors include the Colonial Zone on the western bank of the river, facing the Caribbean Sea.

## Holidays in Santo Domingo

### Santo Domingo: a colorful visitor destination!

A little farther west lies Santo Domingo's historic neighboring district, Gazcue, with many Victorian-style houses and leafy streets. Nearby are the National Theatre, the museum at Plaza de la Cultura, the National Palace, where the government now meets, and the Palace of Fine Arts. Most hotels, restaurants and tourist entertainment can be found along George Washington Avenue, better known as El Malecón. Santo Domingo is a meeting place of European, African and Indigenous traditions. Vibrant, bustling and full of character, the city invites visitors to enjoy tropical scenery, explore the mysteries of history and experience Caribbean life.

## Plaza de Armas and La Moneda Palace: what to see in Santiago, Chile

Santiago de Chile has fascinating historic, residential and business districts. Walk through the historic centre and you will see Plaza de Armas (the "Square of Arms"), with a monument to the city's founder, Pedro de Valdivia, as well as the "Freedom of America" monument and a memorial to Chile's first cardinal, José María Caro. The Presidential Palace of La Moneda, the largest neoclassical building from the conquistador era, the cathedral and the Central Post Office impress visitors with their refined architecture. You can stroll along the capital's main street, through the wooded park on San Cristóbal Hill and into the bohemian Bellavista district. The city's modern commercial and residential architecture is also worth exploring.

Santiago is the capital of Chile and one of the largest cities not only in the country but in all of South America. Many travel routes begin here. Visitors can walk through Plaza de Armas, see the Governors' House, the Central Post Office, the municipality and the Royal Audiencia building, attend a performance at the Opera and Ballet Theatre, explore the city museums and admire La Moneda Palace.

The famous Concha y Toro vineyards are about a 45-minute drive from the capital. Wine cellars are also located here in a century-old park in the Pirque area. First, you will visit Don Melchor and enjoy panoramic views across the Pirque region. Then, of course, in the wine cellars you will be offered Casillero del Diablo wine, known for its refined bouquet and taste. You will learn about winemaking, from the vine to the fermentation of grape juice and the resulting wine with its distinctive aroma and flavor.

## Santiago's visitor districts

### Santiago: an ideal city for travelers!

Santiago is an excellent city from a visitor's point of view. Historic monuments and major attractions are concentrated in the centre. Plaza de Armas is surrounded by grand, historic government buildings that offer a sense of the colonial Spanish architectural style. Travelers who enjoy bohemian nightlife should head to Bellavista, a picturesque district sometimes compared with Montmartre. The quieter Quinta Normal district, also in central Santiago, has several interesting museums and beautiful, peaceful green parks. Ñuñoa is a little corner of England, recalling Santiago in the nineteenth century. Las Condes, Santiago's most modern district, impresses with its many soaring skyscrapers. Welcome to Santiago de Chile!

## Santiago de Cuba: a city of carnivals!

Santiago de Cuba welcomes visitors with tropical vegetation, beautiful sandy beaches, warm seas and consistently sunny weather. Some of Cuba's most colorful carnivals take place here. You can visit Castillo del Morro, described as the world's only Museum of Piracy.

Santiago's central square, Parque Céspedes, formerly Plaza de Armas, is one of its most beautiful squares.

## Santiago de Cuba: a colorful Cuban city!

The city spreads across hills, and its winding streets rise and fall to reveal distinctive views. Padre Pico is a picturesque staircase street with a panoramic view of the city from the top. About 25 km from Santiago, the white church of El Cobre rises above the forest on a hillside: the Basilica of Our Lady of Charity, with a wooden sculpture of the saint. At Baconao Park, visitors can see life-size figures of dinosaurs and Stone Age people.

The historic centre of São Luís was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1997. The city was founded by the French in the seventeenth century before coming under Portuguese control; this history remains visible in its street plan and architecture.

For Ada Tours itineraries, São Luís is particularly useful as a gateway to Lençóis Maranhenses. Visitors can spend time exploring the historic centre, markets and local cuisine before or after a trip to the dunes and lagoons.

Architecture here reflects different periods of the city's development: historic buildings and churches stand alongside dense modern construction and skyscrapers. A visit can focus on art, urban history and gastronomy, with time set aside for individual neighborhoods and evening events.

São Paulo is also an important business destination for Ada Tours. The city already features in corporate travel and delegation programs, where sightseeing is combined with meetings, interpreters, transport and visits to suppliers.
